Bogaudio-VCO: Oscillator with square, saw, triangle and sine running at once, each on its own output
Large knob at the top, marked in volts — sets the pitch, with 0V giving C4 at 261.63Hz
FINE — trims the pitch up to a semitone either way
SLOW — drops the whole pitch range by seven octaves, so the module runs as an LFO
LINEAR — frequency follows the pitch voltage at 1000Hz per volt rather than an octave per volt, and the oscillator stops at 0V
PW — sets the pulse width of the square wave, with a 50% square at noon
FM — sets how deeply the FM jack modulates the frequency
EXP and LIN — the switch beside the FM knob picks exponential modulation or linear through-zero modulation
V/OCT — pitch at a volt per octave, added to the frequency knob; the channels patched here set the oscillator's polyphony
SYNC — a rising edge here hard-syncs the oscillator, restarting its cycle
PW jack — modulates the width of the square wave
Four output jacks marked with wave symbols — square, saw, triangle and sine, all from the same oscillator at the same pitch
Menu — DC offset correction, on by default, keeps the square output centred as the pulse width changes; turn it off when using that output as CV
Bogaudio-Pressor: Stereo compressor and noise gate, with a sidechain input and the detector envelope brought out as CV
MODE — COMP attenuates signal above the threshold, GATE attenuates signal below it
THRESHOLD — the level the compressor or gate acts at, -24dB to 6dB, where 0dB is the 10V peak-to-peak of a normal oscillator; the knob attenuates the CV at TRSH, which takes 0-10V
RATIO — how hard the attenuation is applied, from 1 to infinity; at the top of its travel the compressor becomes a limiter; the knob attenuates the CV at the RATIO jack, which takes 0-10V
ATTACK — how long the detector takes to follow the input upward, 0 to 500ms; the knob attenuates the CV at ATT, which takes 0-10V
RELEASE — how long the detector takes to follow the input downward, 0 to 2 seconds; the knob attenuates the CV at REL, which takes 0-10V
DETECT — RMS averages the input over a short window, PEAK reads its instantaneous level
KNEE — SOFT gives a gentler turn as the signal crosses the threshold, HARD a sharper one
IN GAIN — cuts or boosts the left and right inputs by up to 12dB before the detector and the compressor, leaving the sidechain alone; the CV at IGN takes -5 to 5V and is added to the knob
OUT GAIN — boosts the left and right outputs by up to 24dB after compression, with soft limiting at plus or minus 12V; the CV at OGN takes -5 to 5V and is added to the knob
IN/SIDE — crossfades what the detector listens to between the L and R inputs at IN and the sidechain at SD
COMPRESSION — the meter down the right side, showing how much attenuation is happening at this moment
L and R — audio in on the left column, out on the right; SIDE takes an external signal for the detector to listen to
ENV — outputs the detector's control signal as CV, rising as the attenuation deepens
Menu — Threshold range doubles the THRESHOLD knob's span, to -48dB through 12dB
Bogaudio-Mult: Multiple, 3HP — copies one signal to three outputs, twice over; polyphonic cables are copied with their channels intact
IN-A — signal into the upper splitter, copied to the three OUT jacks below it
IN-B(A) — signal into the lower splitter; with nothing patched here, IN-A is copied to all six outputs
OUT — the three jacks under each input, each carrying a copy of that input
Bogaudio-Matrix44Cvm: Expander adding a mute button and a CV input for each of the sixteen mix points of a MATRIX44; it must sit directly to the right of the MATRIX44 it serves
MUTE — sixteen buttons in a grid matching the MATRIX44 knobs; a button silences its mix point, overriding both the knob and the CV
MUTE — right-clicking a button solos that mix point and mutes the other fifteen; clicking it again restores the mutes that were set before
CV — sixteen jacks in a grid matching the MATRIX44 knobs, each taking -5 to 5V; the MATRIX44 knob for that mix point attenuverts the CV
Menu — Solo mutes by column confines soloing to one column, so a solo changes only that one output
Bogaudio-Arp: Arpeggiator that collects notes from polyphonic pitch and gate inputs and plays them back one note per clock pulse, monophonically
MODE — UP plays the collected notes from low to high, DN plays them from high to low, IO plays them in the order they arrived
MODE — PD runs the notes up then down without repeating the top and bottom ones, PR runs them up then down and repeats those two
MODE — RD picks notes from the arpeggio at random and may repeat one, SH plays every note once per pass in a random order
GATE knob — sets the length of each output gate as a proportion of the gap between the last two clock pulses, with a minimum of 1ms; fully clockwise the gate never drops between notes
HOLD — latches the arpeggio so it keeps playing after every input gate has fallen; the next gate starts collecting a new one
CLOCK — advances the arpeggio one note per pulse; nothing plays without it
RESET — a trigger here sends playback back to the first note on the next clock
V/OCT input — polyphonic pitch; when a gate arrives on one of its channels, the pitch on that channel is added to the arpeggio
GATE input — polyphonic gates; a gate going high on a channel adds the note from the matching V/OCT channel
V/OCT output — pitch of the note playing now, always monophonic
GATE output — gate for the note playing now, always monophonic
Menu — Use new notes set to Immediately folds freshly played notes into the arpeggio at once rather than waiting for it to restart
Menu — Max gate length set to Fixed makes the GATE knob set a length of 1ms to 500ms outright, ignoring the clock rate
Bogaudio-CVD: Delay built for CV, and usable on audio, from under a millisecond up to ten seconds
TIME — sets the delay time in seconds, multiplied by the scale knob below it; shortening the time truncates what is held in the delay buffer
Small knob under TIME, marked 0.1, 1 and 10 — sets the longest delay TIME can reach, a tenth of a second, one second or ten seconds
CV under TIME — takes 0-10V to control the delay time; the TIME knob attenuates it
DRY/WET — mixes the undelayed signal at D against the delayed signal at W
CV under DRY/WET — takes -5 to 5V to control the dry and wet mix
IN — the signal to be delayed; the channels patched here set the module's polyphony
OUT — the dry and delayed signals mixed as DRY/WET sets them
Bogaudio-Manual: Manual trigger and gate, 3HP — one button driving eight outputs
TRIG — the button; every output sits at 5V for as long as it is held, and 0V the rest of the time
OUT — eight jacks, all carrying the voltage the button is producing
Menu — the high output voltage can be raised from 5V to 10V
Menu — Trigger on load, off by default, sends a 10ms pulse from every output 100ms after the patch starts running
Bogaudio-Analyzer: Four-channel spectrum analyzer, with the traces drawn on the display filling the top of the panel
RANGE — scrolls the span of frequencies drawn: the lowest tenth at full counter-clockwise, the whole range at noon, the top fifth at full clockwise
SMOOTH — averages between 0 and 500ms of analysis frames into the trace; more steadies the picture and adds lag behind the sound
QUALITY — the FFT window size: GOOD is 1024 samples, HIGH is 2048, ULTRA is 4096, each doubled when Rack runs at 96kHz or higher; larger sizes resolve frequency more finely and cost more CPU
WINDOW — the window function applied before the FFT: KAISER, HAMMING, or NONE
IN — four inputs, one per trace; a polyphonic cable has its channels summed before the spectrum is measured
THRU — four outputs, each passing its own input on untouched, polyphonic channels intact
Display — clicking and holding freezes it and puts up a readout of the frequency bin under the pointer and each signal's level there; drag to move the readout along
Menu — the vertical scale can reach down to -120dB instead of -60dB, or be switched to a linear percentage where 100% is 0dB
Menu — the frequency axis can be switched from logarithmic to linear
